title: observability: propagate request-id + traceparent through streaming + openai-compat, add per-endpoint metrics tags and structured logs
author: Asha Patel
description: Context and motivation: production services using the OpenAI-compatible API and the native Redwood API need consistent observability signals for debugging and cost attribution. Streaming responses previously dropped trace headers and request identifiers in chunk envelopes which made correlating client-side traces and server logs difficult. This change adds a request-id middleware, propagates W3C traceparent/tracestate across sync and streaming paths, enriches structured logs with request and trace identifiers, and attaches per-endpoint metrics tags (route, model, openai_compat) for better aggregation. It also updates the OpenAI compatibility layer to reflect X-Request-ID semantics and ensures function-calling/structured-output streaming envelopes include the same identifiers. Summary of changes: request-id middleware + header mapping; stream writer now injects request_id and traceparent into SSE/event envelope metadata; OpenAI-compat handler maps X-Request-ID <-> internal request_id and preserves traceparent; per-route metrics tagging in observability layer; structured log formatter updated to always include request_id/trace_id/span_id; integration tests for streaming observability; docs update for OpenAI compatibility behavior. Backwards compatibility notes: header names are additive; clients that rely on previous chunk payloads are unaffected except they will now see additional metadata in the chunk-level envelope. No API contract breaking changes to request/response JSON payloads for non-streaming calls. Related work: references ENG-9821 (observability initiative) and previous PRs that added request id in non-streaming paths.

review_comments: Diego Morales (review): Please confirm that the traceparent propagation is robust across HTTP/2 multiplexed streams and that we aren't reusing the same span ids when chunks are retried.
Asha Patel (author): Confirmed - extraction/propagation uses W3C trace headers and the stream writer reads the ctx trace directly. Added unit tests to assert unique span ids for retried chunks.
Jian Li (review): Linter flagged exported function docs in metrics/tags.go, also please add a small benchmark for the tags lookup in high-cardinality routes.
Asha Patel (author): Fixed docs and added micro-benchmark; results show negligible overhead (~0.2% latency on p95 for tagging path).
Morgan Chen (review): Integration test failing intermittently in CI due to a race in the test harness that reads logs; suggest making the test resilient to log ordering.
Asha Patel (author): Made the test idempotent and order-agnostic; CI rerun green.
merge_summary: Squash merged after approvals from Diego, Jian, and Morgan. CI green after flakiness fix in integration tests. No follow-on migrations required.
release_notes: Added request ID propagation and traceparent support for streaming endpoints; structured logs now include request_id and trace_id; per-endpoint metrics tags enable better aggregation for cost and latency dashboards. OpenAI compatibility layer now preserves X-Request-ID and includes it in streaming chunk metadata.
